findings.detail: Access-control design is strong: Decision 5 / AC require ProjectService.requireOwned(ownerId, projectId, false) FIRST on every project-scoped endpoint, uniform 404 for foreign/soft-deleted/invalid projectId|funnelId, top-level projectId on funnel_executions for cross-project isolation and cascade, and an IT ('requireOwned + cross-project isolation (uniform 404)'). funnelId is always resolved within the owned projectId scope, preventing IDOR across projects. No access-control weakness found in the proposed architecture — this is a NON-ISSUE recorded for completeness.
findings.recommendation: Keep requireOwned as the FIRST statement (before any funnel/execution lookup) in every controller method, including activate and delete. Ensure the funnelId lookup is always constrained by the owned projectId (findByIdAndProjectId), not by _id alone, so a valid funnelId from another project yields the uniform 404 rather than leaking existence. Add an explicit IT asserting that GET/PATCH/DELETE of a funnelId belonging to another owner's project returns 404 (not 403), matching the existing AppException uniform-404 idiom.

findings.detail: Decision 10 correctly distinguishes author markup (left as-is) from substituted variable values (escaped per HTML/MarkdownV2 rules), which is the right anti-injection model for Telegram templating — a subscriber-controlled {user.first_name}='x' or '*x*' cannot break out into markup or inject formatting/entities. However, Decision 10 and Task 2 name only SEND_MESSAGE text. The SEND_IMAGE 'caption' field is also parseMode-aware and supports {variables} (per Data Models), so it is an equally exploitable injection sink if it does not route through the SAME VariableTemplateRenderer escaping path.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly state (Decision 10 + Task 6 SendImage executor) that the SEND_IMAGE caption is rendered through the identical VariableTemplateRenderer with parseMode-aware escaping of substituted values, identical to SEND_MESSAGE text. Add a unit test in the renderer/executor suite asserting caption variable escaping for HTML and MarkdownV2 (mirror the SendMessage escaping tests). Verify the MarkdownV2 escape set covers the full Telegram-required character set (_ * [ ] ( ) ~ ` > # + - = | { } . !) and HTML escapes <, >, & — incomplete escape tables are the usual real bug here.

findings.detail: SEND_IMAGE takes an arbitrary owner-supplied imageUrl that is passed as a URL string to Telegram's sendPhoto. The fetcher is Telegram's servers, NOT our backend (sendPhoto with a URL never causes our process to dereference the URL), so the classic SSRF impact (our server reaching internal metadata endpoints / internal network) does NOT apply here — this is correctly out of scope as a server-side SSRF against our infrastructure. Residual concern: imageUrl receives no scheme/format validation in the spec, so non-http(s) schemes or malformed URLs reach Telegram and simply produce a terminal failure -> execution failed. The actor is the authenticated project owner (not an anonymous user), which further limits abuse.
findings.recommendation: Add lightweight server-side validation of imageUrl at save/activate time: require https:// (or http(s)://) scheme and a syntactically valid URL, reject file:/ftp:/data: and other schemes with 422. This is defense-in-depth and improves UX (fail at edit time, not mid-funnel). Do NOT fetch the URL server-side to 'pre-validate' it — that would INTRODUCE real SSRF; validation must be scheme/format-only.

findings.category: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
findings.detail: Observability is logs-only (JobRunr dashboard disabled) and the AC mandates logging every state transition; Decision 6 also swallows+logs all fire() errors. This is good for auditability but creates a sensitive-data-in-logs risk: rendered message bodies, SEND_IMAGE captions, custom field values, and {user.*} substitutions can contain subscriber PII (names, usernames, arbitrary custom-field content). The spec states 'no token/secret leakage in logs' but does not address PII or full rendered-content logging. Under GDPR, indefinitely retained logs containing subscriber PII are a compliance concern.
findings.recommendation: Specify a logging policy: log structural/state identifiers (funnelId, executionId, subscriberId, stepType, currentStepIndex, status transition, terminal reason code) but NOT the rendered message text, caption, or substituted variable values. For the swallow+log in fire() and step-executors, log exception class + message + identifiers, never the rendered payload. Add a log-content review item to Task 12 (security audit) asserting no rendered SEND_MESSAGE/caption body or custom-field value is emitted at INFO.

findings.detail: TelegramSender.sendPhoto (Decision 13) reuses the existing token-decrypt path and POSTs to /bot{token}/sendPhoto, i.e. the decrypted bot token is embedded in the request URL/path. This is a new call site for the token; if the RestClient request URI (including path) is ever logged — directly, via an HTTP client interceptor, or in an exception/stack trace on 4xx/5xx/timeout — the bot token leaks into logs. The existing sendText already handles this, but sendPhoto is a new surface.
findings.recommendation: Ensure sendPhoto inherits the exact token-redaction discipline of sendText: never log the full request URI; on 429/5xx/403/timeout the error logs must use a redacted endpoint (e.g. '/bot***/sendPhoto') and never echo the token. Add an assertion in the Task 3 TelegramSender test that a failing sendPhoto does not place the token into any log output. Confirm decrypted tokens are not retained in DTOs or audit records written by dispatchSubscriberHook.

findings.detail: Two amplification vectors are only partially mitigated. (1) Sweep batch size: the spec relies on the (status,nextRunAt) index and 'batch atomic-claim' but does not define a per-tick claim/processing CAP. On a large funnel_executions base a single PT30S tick could attempt to claim and run an unbounded number of executions, contending Mongo and the Telegram sender. (2) Self-inflicted Telegram flood: 'consecutive NON-Delay steps run within one tick (while loop)'. An owner can author a funnel of up to FUNNEL_MAX_STEPS=50 back-to-back SEND_MESSAGE/SEND_IMAGE steps; combined with allow_re_enter=true and bursty /start traffic this becomes a rapid message flood toward subscribers and toward the Telegram API (risking bot-level 429 / temporary bans). The /start rate-limit (100/min) caps START frequency but not the per-execution fan-out of no-delay steps.
findings.recommendation: (1) Add an explicit per-tick claim limit / pagination (e.g. FUNNEL_SWEEP_BATCH_SIZE) so each PT30S tick processes a bounded number of executions; document it as an env var alongside FUNNEL_SCHEDULER_INTERVAL_SECONDS. (2) Add a guard against unbounded no-delay step bursts: either a max consecutive non-Delay step count per tick (yield back to nextRunAt after N sends) or rely on documenting that TelegramSender's 429 backoff naturally throttles — and add an IT asserting the while-loop terminates and respects rate-limit backoff. (3) Confirm allow_re_enter=true cannot be used to spin executions faster than the /start rate-limit by an automated client.

findings.detail: Input validation is well specified and constrained: tagSlug ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$, trigger/deep-link payload <=64 chars [A-Za-z0-9_-], text <=4096 (trim-not-fail after substitution), Delay >=1 minute (422 otherwise), FUNNEL_MAX_STEPS=50, custom field value via CustomFieldValueValidator, per-type required-field validation via @Valid on DTOs. These close the common injection/overflow vectors at the boundary. Recorded as a NON-ISSUE confirming the validation design is sound; the only gap is the imageUrl/caption items flagged separately.
findings.recommendation: Enforce ALL listed constraints server-side at save AND activate time (not only via frontend vee-validate/zod), since the engine consumes the snapshot directly. Ensure post-substitution length handling (trim to 4096) also applies to SEND_IMAGE caption (Telegram caption limit is 1024, not 4096) — validate caption against the correct Telegram caption limit, which the spec currently does not specify.

findings.detail: The at-most-once design (Decision 4: findAndModify CAS claim before send + per-step pending->in_progress->done), the re-enter unique partial index (Decision 8), bot pinning (Decision 7), snapshot isolation (Decision 3), pre-send status gating, and fire() swallow+log isolation (Decision 6) collectively form a coherent threat model against duplication, race, and webhook retry-storm. Using .name() literals for enum values in findAndModify criteria (Decision 14) correctly avoids index byte-mismatch. No security defect in the concurrency model; recorded as NON-ISSUE.
findings.recommendation: Keep the integration tests that assert the two-replica atomic-claim race (BotConnectRaceIT pattern) and idempotent re-run of a claimed step as release gates. Verify the unique partial index filter exactly matches status IN [running, waiting] so a cancelled/failed/completed execution does not block a legitimate re-enter, and that DuplicateKey is swallowed only for the re-enter no-op path (not masking other write errors).

summary: Tech-spec architecture review (no code yet) against OWASP Top 10. The security design is generally strong: anti-IDOR (requireOwned-first + uniform 404 + cross-project isolation), markup-injection-safe templating (escape substituted values, preserve author markup), well-constrained input validation (tag slug/trigger payload/text/delay), and a coherent concurrency/at-most-once threat model (atomic claim, re-enter unique index, bot pinning, snapshot, fire() isolation). SSRF is correctly out of scope because Telegram (not our backend) fetches the SEND_IMAGE URL. No critical or high findings. Recommended changes before/during implementation (medium): (1) route SEND_IMAGE caption through the same escaping path as message text and use the correct 1024 caption limit; (2) define a logging policy that excludes rendered message bodies / subscriber PII from the logs-only observability and swallow+log paths (GDPR); (3) guarantee bot-token redaction on the new sendPhoto call site (token sits in the URL path); (4) add a per-tick sweep batch cap and guard against unbounded no-delay step bursts / re-enter amplification to prevent self-inflicted Telegram flood and Mongo contention. Low: add scheme/format-only validation of imageUrl at save time (do NOT server-side fetch it). Verdict issues_found reflects medium-severity hardening items; there are zero critical findings, so this does not block the feature from proceeding once the medium items are folded into the relevant tasks (notably Task 2/3/6 and the Task 12 security audit checklist).
